item.name: Navivox stdio protocol control-plane tracer
item.contract: `gormes navivox serve --stdio` exposes a Gormes-owned SSH stdio control-plane server for the future Flutter Navivox app. The first slice implements only the binary NVOX frame codec and fakeable server loop for `hello` -> `server.status`, `ping` -> `pong`, and unknown readable event -> structured `error`; it rejects bad magic, unsupported prelude versions, invalid JSON headers, oversized headers/payloads, and payload-length mismatches without starting gateway.Manager or handling chat, voice, config, tools, pairing, or selected-agent routing.
item.degraded_mode: Unreadable framing errors close the stdio server with typed Go errors instead of emitting untrustworthy in-band frames; readable unsupported event types return redacted `error` frames with correlation_id set to the triggering message id.
ready_when: The decision record defines NVOX magic, protocol v1, header length, JSON header, payload_length, JSON-vs-binary body placement, and unsupported-version policy.
Tests can use bytes.Buffer or an in-memory pipe; no SSH daemon, PTY, Flutter app, gateway.Manager, provider, or live channel SDK is required.
not_ready_when: The slice attempts `chat.submit` gateway dispatch, selected-agent routing, config.schema/admin, tool-call events, pairing roles, voice/TTS/STT, SSH client logic, or Flutter UI integration.
The implementation treats Navivox as a Hermes platform enum parity port instead of a Gormes-owned first-party channel.
Bad magic, invalid headers, or unsupported prelude versions are answered with in-band frames instead of failing the untrusted stream.
acceptance: Codec tests prove binary frames round-trip with ASCII NVOX magic, uint32 network-byte-order protocol/header lengths, JSON headers, exact payload_length handling, and byte-for-byte binary payload preservation.
Codec tests prove bad magic, unsupported prelude version, invalid JSON, oversized header/payload, and payload-length mismatch return typed errors.
Server tests prove `hello` returns `server.status` with protocol=1, feature list, version/config evidence, and correlation_id matching the hello message id.
Server tests prove `ping` returns `pong` with correlation_id and unknown readable event types return a structured redacted `error` frame.
cmd/gormes tests prove `gormes navivox serve --stdio` is registered, requires `--stdio`, and can complete a fake stdio handshake without PTY assumptions.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-05: TDD added internal/channels/navivox with the NVOX binary frame codec, typed framing errors, static status provider, and fakeable server loop. `gormes navivox serve --stdio` is registered as a thin command and handles hello/server.status, ping/pong, unknown readable event errors, EOF shutdown, and bad framing rejection without starting gateway.Manager, SSH, providers, Flutter, chat, config, tool, pairing, or voice surfaces.
done_signal: Navivox frame codec and stdio control-plane fixtures prove fake clients can handshake and health-check the server before chat, config, tool, or voice rows begin.

provenance.note: Navivox is a Gormes-owned first-party Flutter/SSH channel. Hermes gateway sources inform manager/channel principles, but there is no upstream Hermes Navivox platform to port.

item.name: Navivox QR pairing descriptor CLI
item.contract: `gormes navivox pair` creates a gateway pairing-code request for the `navivox` platform, prints a terminal QR code, and prints a plain-text fallback `navivox://pair?...` descriptor containing transport=ssh, host, port, SSH user, `gormes navivox serve --stdio`, protocol version, device name, pairing code, and expiry. Host selection prefers an explicit `--host`, then Tailscale IPv4, then LAN IPv4, then loopback. `gormes navivox setup-host --plan` renders the recommended host preparation path with Tailscale SSH, OpenSSH server commands, and sudo-password safety without mutating the host.
item.degraded_mode: If QR scanning is unavailable, the fallback URI is fully usable. If Tailscale is unavailable, the command still emits an explicit host source and recommends `gormes navivox setup-host --plan`. Pairing output never includes private keys, sudo passwords, or shell credentials; setup planning states that sudo passwords are prompt-only and never stored.
source_refs: Context7 /websites/tailscale: `tailscale up --ssh` and `tailscale set --ssh` for secure remote SSH
ready_when: The prior Navivox stdio control-plane tracer is complete.
Gateway pairing store can issue and persist pending platform codes without live network credentials.
QR rendering can be tested with text fallback and no live SSH daemon.
not_ready_when: The slice attempts live SSH login, authorized_keys mutation, Tailscale installation, config admin, selected-agent routing, or chat gateway binding.
The QR contains a sudo password, private key, API token, or other credential that grants shell access.
The CLI claims that pairing approval is enforced by `serve --stdio` before the Navivox channel-binding row validates that behavior.
unblocks: Navivox host setup apply with transient sudo
Navivox Flutter QR scanner and SSH bootstrap
acceptance: `gormes navivox pair --host 100.77.1.2 --port 2222 --user ada --device-name pixel-lab --qr=false` prints a clear operator-first pairing screen, server details, pairing code, fallback URI, and Tailscale recommendation.
The fallback URI parses as `navivox://pair` and contains transport, host, port, user, command, protocol, code, and device fields.
The command persists one pending `navivox` pairing record in the existing gateway pairing store.
Pairing output does not contain sudo-password prompts, private-key markers, or credential-shaped text.
`gormes navivox setup-host --plan` renders Tailscale install/up guidance, OpenSSH server enable commands, and a clear statement that sudo passwords are prompt-only and never stored.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-05: TDD added `gormes navivox pair` with qrterminal rendering, text fallback, explicit host/port/user/command details, existing gateway pairing-store persistence, Tailscale-first host discovery, and `setup-host --plan` UX copy for OpenSSH/Tailscale/sudo safety. Live privileged host mutation remains a separate planned row.
done_signal: Operators can run one command on the Gormes host, scan a QR from Navivox, or manually paste a complete SSH stdio pairing descriptor without exposing credentials.

provenance.upstream_ref: OpenClaw channel pairing challenge helpers and Tailscale-first remote-access docs; Hermes QR onboarding and network hardening guidance
provenance.note: Navivox QR pairing is Gormes-owned. OpenClaw proves channel pairing challenge UX and Tailscale-first remote access patterns; Hermes contributes QR terminal onboarding precedent and the security rule to avoid public exposure without VPN/Tailscale/firewall.

item.name: Navivox Flutter voice morph surface
item.contract: The Flutter Navivox app exposes a reusable `VoiceMorphSurface` for voice mode with state-driven soft morph graphics, an intensity input that can later bind to mic/TTS amplitude, reduced-motion phase freezing, live semantics, and a visible speaking surface in the fake chat voice message flow.
item.degraded_mode: Reduced-motion settings freeze phase-driven animation without removing the state-specific visual. Intensity is clamped to 0.0..1.0 so malformed audio levels cannot distort layout or painter behavior.

The first slice can use fake state/intensity inputs and does not need real microphone or audio playback plumbing.
not_ready_when: The slice starts live microphone capture, TTS playback, SSH streaming, or provider audio work.
The widget requires golden screenshots to prove basic behavior, ignores reduced-motion, or exposes no semantics for blind users.

The painter receives clamped intensity and deterministic phase/style inputs that can later be driven by real audio amplitude.

item.name: Navivox host setup apply with transient sudo
item.contract: `gormes navivox setup-host --apply` prepares a Linux host for Navivox by detecting OpenSSH server and Tailscale readiness, prompting for sudo password only through a masked transient prompt when required, installing/enabling OpenSSH server and Tailscale through explicit distro-aware steps, running `tailscale up --ssh` or equivalent Tailscale SSH enablement with operator confirmation, and discarding the sudo password immediately after the command. The existing `--plan` output remains the non-mutating default evidence surface.
item.degraded_mode: Unsupported OS, missing package manager, missing systemd, failed sudo, failed Tailscale auth, or declined confirmation return typed setup evidence and leave the host unchanged beyond steps already completed. The command never writes sudo passwords, private SSH keys, or Tailscale auth keys into config, progress data, logs, or pairing URIs.
ready_when: Navivox QR pairing descriptor CLI is complete.
The setup executor can be injected in tests so no real sudo, package manager, systemctl, curl, or Tailscale command runs in CI.
The UX contract distinguishes Tailscale installation/enablement, OpenSSH installation, service enablement, and QR pairing handoff.
not_ready_when: The command silently runs curl-pipe-shell, installs Tailscale during normal `install.sh`, stores sudo password or Tailscale auth keys, modifies `authorized_keys` without explicit approval, or opens public SSH/firewall rules by default.
Tests require root, network, a live Tailscale account, package manager access, or a real SSH daemon.
The implementation bypasses the existing Gormes secret/sudo prompt language or writes a second host-setup state model outside the canonical config/runtime surfaces.
unblocks: Navivox Flutter first-run remote host preparation
acceptance: `gormes navivox setup-host --plan` remains non-mutating and lists every command category that `--apply` may run.
`--apply` prompts before privileged work, masks sudo input, runs commands through an injected executor in tests, and never logs or persists the sudo password.
Linux Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL fixtures cover OpenSSH install/enable command selection and Tailscale install/up command selection.
Unsupported OS/package-manager/systemd fixtures produce actionable setup evidence instead of partial hidden failure.
Post-apply output tells the operator to run `gormes navivox pair` and prefers the Tailscale host/IP in the descriptor.
item.note: Complete 2026-05-05: TDD added `gormes navivox setup-host --apply` behind explicit opt-in confirmation/`--yes`, command previews with shell-quoted copyable commands, distro-aware Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL OpenSSH install/enablement, Tailscale install/`tailscale up --ssh` steps, transient sudo stdin handling through injected command execution seams, unsupported-OS no-change output, and final `gormes navivox pair` handoff. The command never stores sudo passwords or places them in command args/output.
done_signal: Hermetic host-setup fixtures prove `--apply` can prepare SSH/Tailscale using prompt-only sudo handling and leave the operator at a ready-to-scan `gormes navivox pair` handoff.

provenance.upstream_ref: OpenClaw Tailscale-first host setup docs plus Hermes sudo prompt and network-hardening guidance
provenance.note: Navivox host setup is a Gormes-owned explicit operator flow informed by OpenClaw's Tailscale-first setup docs and Hermes sudo/network-hardening guidance.

not_ready_when: The slice stores raw audio by default without an explicit retention policy.
The slice adds outbound campaigns, phone numbers, retries, scheduling, or human transfer.
The slice reports fake token cost when provider usage is absent.
acceptance: A fake Navivox text turn produces a durable run record with transcript, status, timestamps, session id, and provider usage when available.
A fake Navivox voice turn records device transcript, optional server STT evidence, audio duration/codec metadata, and TTS metadata without persisting raw audio unless explicitly configured.

item.name: Navivox per-profile BYO voice profiles
item.contract: Add per-profile voice metadata that lets operators choose STT/TTS providers, voice id, language policy, fallback voice, and safe provider credentials through Gormes config/admin surfaces. Navivox renders voice metadata on profile create/edit and sends voice turns using the active profile; Gormes resolves BYO STT/TTS providers from existing provider matrices and write-only secret references. Local microphone behavior, command word, calibration, auto-send, aliases, and pins remain Navivox app settings, not server profile config.
item.degraded_mode: When a requested STT/TTS provider is unavailable, Gormes records provider_unavailable evidence, falls back according to the profile policy, and keeps text chat usable; secrets remain redacted/write-only.
ready_when: `Navivox natural-language profile seed flow` has landed so profiles have editable draft metadata.
`Navivox safe config admin over HTTP` has landed so provider/secret changes use server-side validation and write-only secrets.
`Navivox voice run records` has landed or is in progress so STT/TTS evidence can be audited.
not_ready_when: The slice stores provider API keys directly in profile metadata or Flutter state.
The slice hardcodes one vendor voice path instead of reusing existing STT/TTS provider matrices.
The slice makes voice mandatory for text chat or first-run connect-and-talk.
The slice stores local command word, calibration, pins, aliases, or trusted-server state in server profile config.
blocked_by: Navivox safe config admin over HTTP
acceptance: Profile metadata supports a voice_profile with stt_provider, tts_provider, voice_id, language_policy, fallback_voice, and credential status refs.
Validation rejects unknown providers and accepts configured local/cloud providers using the existing TTS/STT provider matrices.
Navivox profile create/edit UI can set and display voice profile fields without reading secret values.
A fake voice turn proves Gormes resolves the selected profile and records fallback evidence when the primary provider is unavailable.
test_commands: sh -c 'cd flutter-navivox/app && flutter test test/features/profiles test/features/config test/features/voice'
done_signal: Each Navivox/Gormes profile can carry safe editable BYO STT/TTS voice metadata, voice turns resolve through it, local app voice settings stay local, and text chat remains usable when voice providers degrade.
